title: 'Time traveller' from 2045 has very bad news for humanity and it's coming soon
excerpt: In a resurfaced video, self-styled time traveller Adam Archon predicted an August 2028 alien landing and public time travel that year
content:
In a resurfaced video, self-styled time traveller Adam Archon predicted an August 2028 alien landing and public time travel that year

07:00, 24 Sep 2026Updated 09:36, 24 Sep 2026

A self-proclaimed time traveller from the year 2045 is making remarkable claims about what we can anticipate witnessing over the coming two decades.

‌

A man calling himself Adam Archon presented a string of unsubstantiated forecasts in a March 2019 video that has lately re-emerged online, after the Pentagon's release of UFO documents.

‌

Despite lacking any corroborating proof, he insists he was born on December 6, 2019.

‌

US super-eruption will leave survivors eating insects and seaweed, life here came from out there, docs cure cancer by hacking cells, and Jesus could have been a magic mushroom - all this and more in our weird science newsletter

According to this mysterious character, time travel technology will become accessible to ordinary people in 2028. He additionally asserted that aliens would land on Earth that same year, putting an end to decades of 'global governmental secrecy.'

During a chat on a YouTube channel called Apex TV, Archon appeared with his face hidden and his voice altered to share his supposed experiences.

He claimed that journeying back through time to observe crucial historical moments first-hand would become routine in the future, mentioning that he himself had travelled back to an era before his own birth.

Archon claimed that time travel technology was initially created in 1981 but remained concealed until its public revelation in 2028.

‌

He proceeded to propose that the overwhelming majority of contemporary UFO encounters are actually vessels operated by future time travellers exploring important moments across history.

While supposedly being subjected to polygraph monitoring, Archon declared, "Yes, it is true that aliens did land on Earth in August 2028. In fact, we have known of the existence of aliens before 2028, but it isn't until 2028 that it becomes public knowledge."

He asserted that an implantable microchip called "The One" would be introduced into people's right hands from February 2029.

‌

This microchip would purportedly enhance health, boost mental capacity, and handle financial transactions, making cash completely obsolete.

Apex TV confirmed that the ten-minute interview, which has racked up over 1.3 million views, demonstrated Archon successfully passing the lie detector examination on every question.

‌

Archon went on to claim that by 2045, scientific breakthroughs would enable the cloning of dinosaurs. This advancement would allegedly lead to the establishment of a genuine "Jurassic Park" accessible to the public.

"You can see T. rex, Triceratops, Velociraptor," he said, suggesting that any ancient creature could be witnessed firsthand.

Archon, who offered no concrete evidence to back up his assertions during the interview, claimed that a fresh digital currency framework would be introduced just before a devastating third occurrence: the downfall of the US government.

‌

He insisted that by 2030, the United States would lose its sovereignty and become part of a unified global administration. This new authority would split the world by continents, positioning the US within "District 3."

He also claimed an artificial intelligence system dubbed "The Light," scheduled for release in 2033, will control this new global regime.

Specialists have highlighted that multiple aspects of his claims were inconsistent and legally impossible within the United States.

‌

In a separate three-minute clip recorded without polygraph equipment present, Archon predicted that 2020 would see the public revelation of a highly controversial robot.

However, there seems to be little proof of any robotic debut that sparked significant worldwide or national debate during that period.

Researchers observe that the physics of time travel into the past align with Einstein's theory of general relativity, which considers space and time as a single, curved "spacetime" affected by gravity.

Nonetheless, despite this theoretical feasibility, no concrete proof exists of technology able to accomplish time travel.
